sd_delicacy_wall.blurb: Delicacy Wall is a steep limestone face in the Shadowlands zone of Spearfish Canyon, a part of the canyon that is a good pick for summer days. Most of the roped climbing is bolted sport, from stout 5.10s up to the low 5.13 range, and there are also a good number of boulder problems from V0 up to around V8. The holds here run larger and the angle more overhanging than much of the canyon's pocket climbing, so expect powerful moves rather than delicate balance, despite the name. Approaches in the canyon are short, usually a quarter hour or less on worn trails. Fall is the best season; spring can be damp.

sd_ice_box.blurb: Ice Box, also called Hellsgate Gulch, is a small, tight gully in Spearfish Canyon and one of the first walls bolted there. Nearly everything is sport climbing on limestone, with most grades between 5.10 and 5.12 and only a few easier warm-ups around 5.9. The routes are short and punchy, and they are protected well enough that most climbers leave the rack at home and carry just draws. The crag sits right beside the road, so the walk from the car is almost nothing, which makes it an easy add-on to a day elsewhere in the canyon. In winter the gulch also draws ice climbers.

_expect.name: Main Wall (China and Victor Charlie Walls), The

sd_main_wall_china_and_victor_charlie_wa.blurb: The Main Wall is the centerpiece of the VC, a limestone canyon southwest of Rapid City known for overhanging, cryptic sport climbing. This is a strong climber's wall: the grades sit almost entirely in the 5.12 and 5.13 range, with only a couple of easier routes, so it rewards fingers and endurance rather than offering a beginner's tick list. Other, milder walls in the canyon suit moderate climbers. Reaching the cliff means hiking down into the canyon and then following the creek bed, which can run cold and wet in spring and early summer, so water shoes are handy. Summers around Rapid City get hot, so plan for cooler hours.

sd_inner_outlet.blurb: Inner Outlet is the large granite formation looming above Sylvan Lake in the Needles of Custer State Park. Nearly all of the climbing is traditional, with a few bolted lines, and the grades run from easy fifth class through the 5.10s and into the 5.12s. The rock is sharp, strong granite, known in the Black Hills for face climbing on quartz-crystal holds, with cracks mixed in among widely spaced bolts, so bring a rack. Routes tend to be bold and run out, and the spire-like formations usually need rappels to get down. A campground sits nearby and the lake draws crowds; early mornings and evenings are quieter and cooler.
sd_inner_outlet.approach: Follow the path along the near shore of Sylvan Lake, pass beneath the huge chockstone, then bear left. The formation comes into view once you round the ridge of rock behind the dam.

sd_indecent_exposure.blurb: Indecent Exposure is a sport wall in the Blue Sky zone of Spearfish Canyon, one of the sections of the canyon with the best-quality stone. The routes are bolted and the grades concentrate in the 5.10 to 5.12 range, with a few 5.13s at the top end and a single 5.9 at the bottom. Expect sustained, continuous climbing rather than a single hard move. Approaches in the canyon are short, typically a quarter hour or less, and many of its walls are most pleasant in the morning or evening, or in the cooler, drier fall months. Spring can be wet.

sd_skeletal_remains.blurb: Skeletal Remains is a small roadside sport crag near the northern, downstream start of Spearfish Canyon, the first climbing area you meet driving in from Spearfish. The rock is limestone, a bit polished from traffic, and the grades spread wider than most of the canyon: easy fifth-class warm-ups through the 5.10s and into the 5.12s, so it suits mixed groups. A few routes can be top-roped. It is a quick-stop wall rather than a destination on its own, handy for a short session or a low-commitment outing. The trail to the base takes about a minute.

sd_thunderhead_the.blurb: The Thunderhead is a very steep limestone wall in the Sunshine zone of Spearfish Canyon, with one of the canyon's biggest clusters of hard routes. It is all sport climbing, with most grades in the 5.12 and 5.13 range and only a few lines easier. Routes open with hard moves on sidepulls and underclings, then settle into long stretches of pockets. The first bolt is often high and the crux can come right at it, so a stick-clip is useful. The wall takes roughly five minutes to reach on a steep hillside trail. The Sunshine area is a favored cool-season destination.

tn_main_wall_3.blurb: Main Wall is the principal cliff at Deep Creek, a forested sandstone gorge in Cumberland Trail State Park near Soddy-Daisy. The climbing is steep, powerful sport on solid, featured sandstone, with most routes at 5.12 and a good number of 5.11s and 5.13s on either side. This is a wall for strong climbers more than newcomers; the milder moderates are on the nearby Tea and Crumpets Wall. Many lines seep from the top in winter and spring, and the lower walls stay wet early in the season, though some stretches of the cliff are dependably dry. The trail crosses the creek and then climbs steeply to the right end of the wall.

tn_upper_leda.blurb: Upper Leda is the largest section of Leda, a small sandstone bluff west of Soddy-Daisy that is popular for after-work sessions and for learning to lead. The rock is mostly very good, and the mix is roughly two-thirds sport and one-third trad, so bring a rack if you want the crack climbs. Grades run from easy fifth class through 5.12, with a healthy block of 5.9 to 5.11 in the middle, and several friendly routes make good first leads. The walk-in is a steady hike on a cut trail.
tn_upper_leda.parking_note: Use the paved lot where Montlake Road bends sharply uphill, directly across from Terrace Falls Drive. Spaces are limited, so sharing rides helps.
tn_upper_leda.approach: A cut trail runs west beneath the power lines to the bluff, a steady walk of roughly 15 to 20 minutes.

tn_middle_obed.blurb: Middle Obed is a sunny, less steep wall just left of the big overhanging Tieranny roofs in the Obed and Clear Creek area. The routes are almost all sport, with a couple of trad lines, and the grades cluster from 5.10 through 5.12 with a few easier and harder outliers. The Obed's Cumberland sandstone is very hard, with good friction and layered features that make jugs and slopers, and most climbers bring draws plus a stick-clip for the high first bolts. Because the wall catches the sun, it is more comfortable in cool weather than in the heat of summer.
